name: The Four Way
tagline: Soul food on Mississippi Boulevard since 1946, a Soulsville gathering place.
description: The Four Way serves soul food plates like fried catfish, smothered chicken and cobbler in Soulsville. It was opened in 1946 by Irene and Clint Cleaves and is now owned by Patrice Bates Thompson. Civil rights leaders ate here, and it still draws a lunch crowd Wednesday through Sunday.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Patrice Bates Thompson named by BuyBlack (Feb 2026) and UACMEM; listed in Taste of Memphis Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 7, 2026). Open: own site with current hours (Wed to Sun). Founded 1946 per UACMEM. Instagram handle from I Love Memphis 2026 list.

name: Cozy Corner BBQ
tagline: North Parkway barbecue known for Cornish hens and ribs, family run since 1977.
description: Cozy Corner smokes ribs, Cornish hens and wings in a pit on North Parkway. Raymond and Desiree Robinson opened it in 1977, and Desiree Robinson was inducted into the American Royal Barbecue Hall of Fame in 2020. Her grandchildren now run it day to day.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Memphis Flyer profile of owner Desiree Robinson; BuyBlack 2026 and Black Dining Week 2026 (Action News 5, Sep 2026). Open: own site with Tue to Sat hours, Sep 2026 Black Dining Week listing. Founded 1977 per Memphis Flyer.

name: Alcenia's
tagline: Downtown soul food and desserts from B.J. Chester-Tamayo, and a warm welcome.
description: Alcenia's serves fried chicken, greens, candied yams and other soul food plates on North Main Street. Owner Betty Joyce "B.J." Chester-Tamayo opened it in 1997 and reopened it in 2022 after a renovation. She is known for greeting guests with a hug.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BLAC Media and BuyBlack (Feb 2026) name owner B.J. Chester-Tamayo. Open: own site with current hours and 2026 footer; in I Love Memphis Jan 2026 list. Instagram left null because the handle could not be confirmed.

name: Payne's Bar-B-Q
tagline: Chopped pork sandwiches with yellow mustard slaw on Lamar Avenue since the 1970s.
description: Payne's is known for its chopped pork shoulder sandwich topped with mustard slaw. Horton and Flora Payne's family started the business in 1972, and their children Ron and Candice Payne run the Lamar Avenue shop today. Flora Payne was honored by the Black Business Association of Memphis.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis piece on Flora Payne's Black Business Association honor, Action News 5 (May 2023), BuyBlack (Feb 2026). Activity: BuyBlack Feb 2026; an Atlas Obscura profile dated Apr 2025 appeared in search results (not opened). No own website found, so null. Zip not confirmed. Sources differ on founding details; 1972 is the most cited year.

name: Uncle Lou's Fried Chicken
tagline: Sweet and spicy fried chicken from Louis Martin, now on Winchester Road.
description: Uncle Lou's serves fried chicken with a sweet and spicy honey glaze, plus sides and pies. Louis "Uncle Lou" Martin opened it in 2001 and has been featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. The restaurant moved from Millbranch Road to Winchester Road.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BuyBlack (Feb 2026) and EDGE Memphis story (Jul 2025) name owner Louis Martin. Moved from 3633 Millbranch to 1725 Winchester (whatnow.com, Mar 2024). Open: own site and Toast ordering live. Founded 2001 per EDGE Memphis.

name: Sage Memphis
tagline: Fusion soul food on South Main from owner Charles Nwankwo.
description: Sage serves what it calls fusion soul cuisine, mixing Southern staples with global flavors, on South Main Street downtown. Owner Charles Nwankwo now also leads Taste of Memphis: Black Dining Week. Sage has taken part in the week for five years.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Daily Memphian (Sep 6, 2026) names owner Charles Nwankwo as leader of Black Dining Week; Action News 5 (Sep 7, 2026) lists Sage. Open: own site with ordering link. Founding year not stated, so null.

name: Eggxactly Breakfast & Deli
tagline: Whitehaven breakfast spot for omelets, chicken and waffles, and deli sandwiches.
description: Eggxactly is a breakfast and deli restaurant on Marlin Road in Whitehaven. Wendell and Adrena Jackson opened it in 2019. It is a regular in Memphis Black Restaurant Week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BLAC Media Black-owned breakfast list; owners Wendell and Adrena Jackson per Daily Memphian. Open: Daily Memphian Jul 2025, Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026), live site. Opened Oct 2019 per Daily Memphian.

name: Curry N Jerk
tagline: Caribbean curry and jerk dishes for dinner downtown on Monroe Avenue.
description: Curry N Jerk cooks Caribbean food, including jerk dishes and oxtails, in downtown Memphis. It is open for dinner several days a week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed in Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026) and I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026); owner not named in sources. Open: own site with current hours.

name: Mahogany River Terrace
tagline: Southern dishes with Creole touches and river views on Mud Island.
description: Mahogany River Terrace serves Southern plates with Creole flavor on Mud Island, looking out over the Mississippi River. It takes reservations and has taken part in Memphis Black Restaurant Week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) and Black Restaurant Week 2025 guide; directory-style proof, owner not confirmed for this location. Open: own site with 2026 menu. Instagram handle from I Love Memphis list.

name: Bala's Bistro
tagline: West African and American plates in Whitehaven from owners with roots in Mali.
description: Bala's Bistro serves jollof rice, lamb saka saka and egusi soup next to burgers and Philly cheesesteaks. Cousins Bala Tounkara and Mady Magassa, who came to Memphis from Mali, opened it in 2019. They also run Mande Dibi West African grill.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners from Mali named by Memphis Magazine and What Now Memphis; listed in BuyBlack (Feb 2026) and Black Restaurant Week 2025. No own website or phone confirmed, so null. Zip not confirmed.

name: A&R Bar-B-Que
tagline: Family barbecue on Elvis Presley Boulevard since 1983, named for Andrew and Rose.
description: A&R serves ribs, pulled pork and barbecue spaghetti. Andrew and Rose Pollard started it in 1983 as a take-out spot, and their children now run the restaurants. It marked 40 years in business in 2023.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Pollard family ownership per Action News 5 (Feb 2023); listed in Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 7, 2026). Own site (spoton) returned 403, so website and phone left null. Zip not confirmed.

name: Memphis Toast
tagline: Breakfast and brunch on Jackson Avenue from North Memphis native Roosevelt Bonds.
description: Memphis Toast serves breakfast, brunch and lunch at 954 Jackson Avenue. Owner and developer Roosevelt Bonds, a North Memphis native, opened it in 2023, and Billy Irby is co-owner.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed in Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026) with co-owners Roosevelt Bonds and Billy Irby; Downtown Memphis Commission project page on Bonds. Phone from Memphis Travel listing. No own website confirmed.

name: Feast & Graze
tagline: Charcuterie boards and grazing tables from owner Cristina McCarter.
description: Feast & Graze builds charcuterie boards, boxes and grazing tables from its shop near Poplar Plaza. Cristina McCarter owns it.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BuyBlack (Feb 2026) names owner Cristina McCarter; I Love Memphis (Jan 2026) list. Open: own site with Tue to Sat hours. Top-up 2026-10-15: dropped 'Rear' so the address geocodes; the entrance is at the rear.

name: Anti Gentrification Cxffee Club
tagline: CxffeeBlack's coffee shop off Bowden Avenue, built around Black coffee history.
description: This is the coffee shop of CxffeeBlack, the Memphis roaster. It serves coffee daily and frames itself as a project to keep coffee money and jobs in Black communities.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed by BuyBlack (Feb 2026) and I Love Memphis (Jan 2026, CxffeeBlack). Open: own page with current address and daily hours, 2026 footer. Phone not listed.

name: SugaShack
tagline: Food and drinks on Beale Street, part of Memphis Black Dining Week.
description: SugaShack is a restaurant on Beale Street downtown. It takes part in Taste of Memphis: Black Dining Week and Black Restaurant Week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: directory and news lists only (Black Dining Week, Action News 5, Sep 2026; I Love Memphis Jan 2026; BRW 2025). Owner and menu details not confirmed, website and phone null. Instagram handle from I Love Memphis list.

name: The Genre
tagline: Lounge and restaurant on Poplar Avenue run by twins Bernard and Lenard Chambers.
description: The Genre is a lounge and restaurant downtown on Poplar Avenue. Twin brothers Bernard and Lenard Chambers own it, and it is part of Black Dining Week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BLAC Media nightlife list (updated Oct 10, 2026) names the Chambers twins; Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026). Own site returned 403, so website null. Phone and zip not confirmed.

name: Salt Bar & Bistro
tagline: Lounge with food, cocktails and live music on South Mendenhall Road.
description: Salt Bar & Bistro is a lounge serving food and drinks with live entertainment in southeast Memphis. It has a dress code.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BLAC Media Black-owned nightlife list (updated Oct 2026) and Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026, as Salt Bistro). Open: own site with 2026 footer and events. Address from BLAC Media; phone and zip not confirmed.

name: 111 Madison
tagline: Downtown restaurant and live music space with weekend brunch.
description: 111 Madison is a downtown restaurant and event space with lunch, dinner and weekend brunch. It hosts live music and private events.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed in Black Dining Week (Action News 5, Sep 2026) and I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026, as One11 Madison); owner not named. Own site has address, phone and hours but no dated posts.

name: Kitchen Laurel
tagline: Cooper-Young breakfast and brunch spot from chef Kevin Sullivan.
description: Kitchen Laurel serves breakfast and brunch on South Cooper, plus catering, take and bake meals and baked goods. Chef Kevin Sullivan runs it with his wife Stacy Sullivan.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof. Open: own site with current hours and 2026 images.

name: Groovy Gratitude
tagline: Uptown juice and smoothie bar with breakfast, wraps and wellness events.
description: Groovy Gratitude makes juices and smoothies in Uptown Memphis. It also hosts yoga events.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof. Own site has address and hours but no dated posts; the Jan 2026 list is the activity proof.

name: Kaye's Pints & Scoops
tagline: Ice cream by the pint and scoop on Winchester Road, Saturdays only.
description: Kaye's sells ice cream by the scoop and the pint from Winchester Road. It is open on Saturday afternoons.

_verified.note: Draft: Black-owned only via I Love Memphis list (Jan 2026). Own site shows Saturday hours but no dated content, and the owner is not named.

name: The Bar-B-Q Shop
tagline: Midtown barbecue on Madison Avenue known for its Dancing Pigs sauce.
description: The Bar-B-Q Shop serves ribs, pulled pork and barbecue spaghetti in Midtown. Frank Vernon and his son Eric Vernon have run it for decades.

_verified.note: Black-owned: MOFAD Legacy Quilt honors Frank and Eric Vernon; BuyBlack (Feb 2026) names Eric Vernon. Activity: BuyBlack Feb 2026 and live site. Opening year conflicts (1983 vs 1987), so null.

name: Hattiloo Theatre
tagline: Black repertory theatre in Overton Square, now in its 20th season.
description: Hattiloo is a freestanding Black repertory theatre in Overton Square, founded in 2006. It stages plays and youth productions year round and is opening its 20th season in 2026 and 2027.

_verified.note: Black institution: Black repertory theatre per own site and WKNO (Apr 2026); in I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026). Open: 2026 and 2027 season shows on own site; Hoodline Jul 2026. Founded 2006 per own site.

name: Stax Museum of American Soul Music
tagline: Museum of Stax Records and soul music on the original Soulsville site.
description: The Stax Museum tells the story of Stax Records and soul music on McLemore Avenue, where the label's studio stood. It also hosts free events and a summer concert series.

_verified.note: Black cultural institution: nonprofit museum of Black soul music history (Soul of America). It is not a privately owned business, so ownership label rests on its mission. Open: own site with Tue to Sun hours; 2026 events on Memphis Travel. Opening year not confirmed, so null. Draft: nonprofit museum, no source says Black-owned or Black-led. Founder decides.

name: Withers Collection Museum & Gallery
tagline: Ernest C. Withers' civil rights and music photographs on Beale Street.
description: The Withers Collection shows the work of photographer Ernest C. Withers, who documented the civil rights movement, the Negro Leagues and Memphis music. It opened on Beale Street in 2011 and is led by his daughter Rosalind Withers. It is on the Tennessee stop of the U.S. Civil Rights Trail.

_verified.note: Black-owned: family-run museum, founder Rosalind Withers named on own site; I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026). Open: own site with current hours; June 2025 exhibit on Memphis Travel. Opened Feb 2011 per Memphis Travel listing.

name: Collage Dance Collective
tagline: Classical ballet company and school centered on Black dancers, based in Binghampton.
description: Collage Dance Collective is a ballet company and academy that describes itself as the largest Black-owned ballet company in the South. It was founded in New York in 2006 by artistic director Kevin Thomas and moved to Memphis in 2007. Its fall 2026 program, ORIGINS, plays at Playhouse on the Square in October.

_verified.note: Black-owned: own site describes it as the largest Black-owned ballet company in the South; Action News 5 profile. Open: RISE at the Cannon Center Feb 2026 (Memphis Travel), ORIGINS Oct 23 to 25 listed on own site.

name: Urevbu Contemporary
tagline: South Main gallery showing contemporary art, including African artists.
description: Urevbu Contemporary is an art gallery in the South Main Arts District. It runs rotating exhibitions.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof; owner not named on own site. Activity: exhibition opened Oct 11, 2025 per own site. Hours not listed.

name: DeMoir Books & Things
tagline: Downtown bookstore from former teacher Jeremee DeMoir, with books for all ages.
description: DeMoir Books & Things sells fiction, nonfiction, comics, graphic novels and children's books. Former teacher Jeremee DeMoir opened it in 2021 and moved it downtown with a grand reopening in May 2024. It has been described as the only Black-owned bookstore in Memphis.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Choose901 (Feb 2022) Black-owned bookstore profile of Jeremee DeMoir. Activity: downtown grand reopening May 2024; I Love Memphis list Jan 2026. Address from Downtown Memphis listing; one I Love Memphis post says 55 S Main, so verify the street direction.

name: Liberty Bank and Trust
tagline: Black-owned bank branch in Whitehaven, successor to Tri-State Bank of Memphis.
description: Liberty Bank and Trust runs a branch on Elvis Presley Boulevard in Whitehaven. Liberty is one of the largest Black-owned banks in the country, and it took over Memphis's Tri-State Bank in 2021.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Liberty's 2021 combination with Black-owned Tri-State Bank of Memphis per Business Wire and Black Enterprise (both seen in search results; Business Wire returned 403 on fetch). Tri-State name retired, so Liberty is the bank row. Open: Memphis branch on Liberty locations page; site has Aug 2026 notices. Branch phone not listed.

name: Pink Noire Beauty Supply & Cosmetics
tagline: Beauty supply and cosmetics store built for Black women, founded by Chasity Monroe.
description: Pink Noire sells hair care, wigs, cosmetics and skin care in a beauty supply store in Bartlett. Founder Chasity Monroe worked in the beauty industry at Procter & Gamble before opening it.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026), directory-style proof; own site names founder Chasity Monroe. Open: own site with store hours and 2026 footer.

name: Bubble Bistro
tagline: Handmade natural soaps, body butters and hair care made in Memphis.
description: Bubble Bistro makes natural body, bath, face and hair products like body butters, soaps, bath bombs and shampoo bars. It sells online.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026); own site links to Essence and Action News 5 Black-owned features (not opened). Open: Sep 2026 reviews and 2026 footer. No storefront address found, so listed as virtual.

name: Royalty Wellness Spa
tagline: East Memphis medspa for facials, body treatments, laser and hair restoration.
description: Royalty Wellness Spa is a medspa offering medical aesthetics, skin care, body treatments, laser work and hair restoration. It is in an office park off Poplar in East Memphis.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof; owner not named. Activity: own site with 2026 footer and the Jan 2026 list.

name: Amani Bath Spa
tagline: South Main spa for mineral baths, massage and body scrubs.
description: Amani Bath Spa offers therapeutic mineral baths, massage including Ashiatsu and couples sessions, body scrubs and facials. Founder Emma Crystal is a licensed massage therapist.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026), directory-style proof; founder Emma Crystal named on own site. Open: own site with current hours and 2026 footer.

name: Jasper Float Spa
tagline: Float tanks, infrared sauna and recovery sessions in a Midtown carriage house.
description: Jasper Float Spa & Wellness Center offers floating, infrared sauna and restorative therapies. It runs from a carriage house on Ellsworth Street and lists a second location on North Main downtown.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof; owner not named. Activity: Jan 2026 list and live site with current hours. Downtown 10 N Main location status unclear on own site, so the Ellsworth address is used.

name: Paula & Raiford's Disco
tagline: Late night disco and dance club downtown on South Second Street.
description: Paula & Raiford's Disco is a late night dance club on South Second Street downtown. It is one of the Black-owned nightlife spots BLAC Media recommends in Memphis.

_verified.note: Black-owned: BLAC Media Black-owned nightlife list (updated Oct 10, 2026) and I Love Memphis (Jan 2026). Old domain now redirects to an unrelated realty site, so website null. Address from BLAC Media; phone and zip not confirmed. Top-up 2026-10-15: wrote Second as 2nd so the address geocodes.

name: Lucyja Hygge
tagline: Midtown metaphysical shop with crystals, candles and Reiki sessions.
description: Lucyja Hygge is a metaphysical shop on Madison Avenue in Midtown. It sells spiritual goods and offers Reiki and intuitive energy healing sessions.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof. Activity: Jan 2026 list and site with 2026 footer. Est. 2021 per own site.

name: City Tasting Box
tagline: Gift boxes of Memphis-made snacks, sweets and sauces, shipped nationwide.
description: City Tasting Box packs gift boxes with snacks, sweets and sauces made by Memphis makers. It ships across the country.

_verified.note: Black-owned: I Love Memphis Black-owned list (Jan 2026) only, directory-style proof; owner not named on own site. Activity: Jan 2026 list and site with 2026 footer. No storefront address, so virtual.

name: The Mane Wildling
tagline: Floral design, event styling and interiors for weddings and events.
description: The Mane Wildling is a floral design and event styling studio that does wedding flowers, event production and interior styling.

_verified.note: Draft: Black-owned only via I Love Memphis list (Jan 2026). Own site footer says 2024 with no newer dated content, and no address or owner is listed.

name: Black Seeds Urban Farms
tagline: North Memphis urban farm growing fruits, vegetables and herbs for nearby neighbors.
description: Black Seeds grows fruits, vegetables and herbs in North Memphis for residents with little access to fresh food. It describes itself as a local food movement.

_verified.note: Draft: Black-owned via Black Farmers Index (Tennessee). Own site footer is 2022 with no newer dated content, so current activity is not confirmed.

name: New Way Aquaponic Farm
tagline: Raleigh aquaponics farm growing greens and herbs and teaching classes.
description: New Way grows leafy greens, herbs and microgreens with aquaponics in Raleigh. It runs classes and orientations for kids and adults and has sold at local farmers markets since opening in 2017.

_verified.note: Draft: Black-owned via Black Farmers Index (Tennessee). Own site states 2017 opening but has no 2024 to 2026 dated content.

name: Black Farmers Market Memphis
tagline: A seasonal South Memphis market where Black farmers sell fresh produce direct.
description: Black Farmers Market Memphis brings Black growers from the Mid-South to the Center for Black Southern Culture in South Memphis. The Black Clergy Collaborative of Memphis started it in 2022 to put fresh food in a neighborhood with few grocery options. The 2026 season ran Tuesday evenings through September.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founded by the Black Clergy Collaborative of Memphis for Black farmers (Tri-State Defender); vendors include Black farms such as Toles Farms. Open: own site lists the 2026 season (opened Sat June 20, then Tuesdays 4 to 7 pm through Sept 22), its 5th season. Seasonal market held at the Center for Black Southern Culture lot, not a single farm.

name: M&B African Food Market
tagline: African groceries in East Memphis, from smoked fish to shea butter.
description: M&B African Food Market stocks grains, flours, seasonings, smoked fish and fresh meats from West, East and Central Africa, plus shea butter. Owner Bala Tounkara came to Memphis from Mali and also runs Bala's Bistro and Mande Dibi, the grill next door.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Bala Tounkara, from Mali (What Now Memphis June 2024, Memphis Magazine). Open: I Love Memphis (Feb 2025) and Choose901 (Mar 2025, gives Suite 5 address). Domain mbafricanmarket.com is for sale, so website null; no phone confirmed. Opening year not confirmed (planned July 2024). Address does not geocode in Nominatim (house number missing), confirmed by two sources.

name: Mbabazi House of Style
tagline: Fair Trade African-inspired clothing, accessories and home decor on Broad Avenue.
description: Mbabazi House of Style sells women's clothing, accessories and home decor inspired by East African design. Founder Grace Byeitima, who is from Uganda, works with seamstresses in Uganda under Fair Trade practices. The shop is in the Broad Avenue Arts District.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Ugandan founder Grace Byeitima profiled by BLAC Media and I Love Memphis. Open: Instagram posts dated Sept 2026, ICIC holiday guide Nov 2024. Address 2553 from own site footer; some directories say 2537 Broad Ave. Founded year conflicts (2005 in BLAC, 2007 in a directory), so null. Price range is an estimate.

name: The African Place
tagline: Uptown Memphis shop for Black books, African imports and natural products since 1999.
description: The African Place sells books on Black history and culture alongside African fabric, clothing, jewelry, musical instruments, incense and natural hair and body products. Trina Clemmons, known as Kikelomo, opened it in 1999 in two houses in Uptown Memphis, and family now runs it.

_verified.note: Black-owned: listed in Book Riot's Black-owned bookstores 2026 (Feb 11, 2026); Action News 5 (2023) notes Oprah Daily named it one of two Black-owned Tennessee bookstores, founded 1999 by Trina Clemmons, now managed by her cousin Darrius Stafford. Open: Book Riot 2026 list and current Downtown Memphis Commission listing (address, phone). No 2024 to 2026 news coverage found; activity proof is list-level only. Website null (Facebook only). Set to draft: the only 2024 to 2026 sign it is open is a list (Book Riot, Feb 2026) and a directory page, no dated activity of its own.

name: Champion's Pharmacy and Herb Store
tagline: Family-run Whitehaven herb store with house-made remedies since 1981.
description: Champion's Pharmacy and Herb Store makes its own herbal tinctures, creams, powders, soaps and blends in house. Dr. Charles Champion, the first Black pharmacist at a Memphis hospital, opened it with his wife Carolyn in 1981, and his daughter Dr. Carol Champion runs it today.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founded by Dr. Charles Champion, first African-American pharmacist at a Memphis hospital (Tri-State Defender, FOX13), now run by his daughter; on I Love Memphis 40+ Black-Owned Businesses (Jan 2026). Open: own site live with shop and (c) 2026, hours Tue to Sat 10 to 2; FOX13 Feb 2024; Memphis Flyer Oct 2024 on a second downtown shop at 65 Monroe Ave, Suite B (not listed here; status unconfirmed). Main store address, ZIP and phone from own site.
